image_description: A close-up, macro photograph of a tiger beetle facing the camera. The beetle has a metallic reddish-bronze head and thorax with iridescent blue-green highlights on the legs and eyes. It features large compound eyes, prominent mandibles, and long antennae. The elytra (wing covers) are visible behind the thorax, showing pale cream-colored markings against a dark background. Six slender legs are visible, planted on a mossy or textured green surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body (head, thorax, start of elytra) suggests an elongated form typical of carabid beetles. The proportions look correct for a tiger beetle.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The exoskeleton exhibits strong metallic iridescence, shifting between bronze/red on the head and blue/green on the legs and eye rims.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The segmentation between head, pronotum, and elytra is clear. The texture appears hard and chitinous.
